answer: I would like to talk about someone at work whom I completely misjudged at first. A quiet person I know well is a colleague of mine who rarely speaks unless he has something worth saying. He handles visa documents at the education consultancy where I work, and we have shared an office for about two years. At first I mistook his silence for coldness, but I soon realised he is simply [[reserved]] rather than unfriendly. As for what he is like, what I have come to appreciate is that when he does speak, people genuinely listen, because his words carry weight. He is an exceptional [[observer]], noticing details in meetings that the more talkative people miss entirely. Once he spotted a small error in a student's visa application that the rest of us had missed for days, which saved the student a great deal of trouble and possibly a rejected visa. I think our culture tends to reward loud, outgoing personalities, so quiet people are often [[overlooked]], which is a shame. Over time I have discovered that he is thoughtful, kind and surprisingly funny once you get to know him. His calm presence is actually quite [[soothing]] in a busy office, especially during the stressful application season. As for how I feel about him, I like and respect him enormously. Honestly, he has taught me that you do not have to be the loudest voice in the room to be respected, and I have a lot of time for him.

followUps.q: Would you describe yourself as quiet?
followUps.answer: Somewhere in the middle, I think. I can be talkative with people I know well, but in new situations I prefer to listen and [[get the measure of]] people before saying much.

followUps.q: Do you think quiet people make good leaders?
followUps.answer: Yes, they can be excellent leaders. They often listen carefully and think before acting, which leads to better decisions. Leadership is not only about speaking loudly; it is about earning respect.

note: Set him at my consultancy, added how I know him, a visa-application example of his observation skills and a clear 'how I feel' line.
